name: Ben Alder Cottage Bothy (MBA)
description: Historic Mountain Bothies Association stone shelter beneath Ben Alder on the remote shores of Loch Ericht. Fireplace and sleeping platforms.

name: Loch Rannoch Water Access
description: Clear freshwater shoreline access along Loch Rannoch. Requires standard backcountry water filtration.

name: Blackburn Bothy (MBA)
description: MBA shelter located along the northern descent of Corrieyairack Pass towards Fort Augustus.

name: River Oykel Water Point
description: Perennial freshwater gravel bar access along River Oykel. Water filtration recommended.

name: Loch Stack Shoreline Water
description: Clean mountain runoff lake at the base of Ben Stack. High-yield filtration source.

name: Glendhu Bothy (MBA)
description: Two-storey MBA bothy nestled at the head of sea loch Loch Glendhu beneath dramatic cliffs. Excellent emergency storm shelter.

name: Glencoul Bothy (MBA)
description: Classic stone MBA bothy on the tidal shore of Loch Glencoul opposite Britain's highest waterfall, Eas a' Chual Aluinn.

name: Suileag Bothy (MBA)
description: Spacious MBA stone cottage in Glencanisp Forest under the sandstone monolith of Suilven. Running burn alongside for water.

name: Loch Assynt Water Access
description: Pristine loch water access near Ardvreck Castle ruins. Filter before consumption.

name: Shenavall Bothy (MBA)
description: World-famous MBA whitewashed bothy in the heart of the Fisherfield Wilderness between An Teallach and Beinn Dearg Mor. Adjacent mountain river for water.

name: Loch na Sealga Water Access
description: Fisherfield wilderness water source flowing from high Torridonian sandstone peaks. Reliable flow year-round.

name: Loch Maree Water Access
description: Deep freshwater mountain loch along Beinn Eighe National Nature Reserve. Safe to filter.

name: Camban Bothy (MBA)
description: Remote National Trust for Scotland / MBA stone shelter at the watershed between Glen Affric and Kintail.

name: Lairig Leacach Bothy (MBA)
description: MBA mountain shelter high in the pass between the Grey Corries and Stob Ban. Emergency shelter and mountain burn.

name: River Fillan Water Access
description: Gentle river access near St Fillan's Priory ruins approaching Tyndrum finish.
